description:
Akhil StrÃ¶mqvist is lean and somewhat raccoon-eyed from chronic sleep debt, with warm medium-brown skin, close-cropped hair, and a habit of wearing a battered optical recording array mounted over his left ear that he has modified so many times it is no longer recognizably a consumer product. His right arm has a functional color-shifting skin mod â€” not cosmetic in origin, repurposed from a Helix Biosystems agricultural camouflage prototype he acquired through means he prefers not to specify â€” that he uses as an on-body production notes display. When he is thinking through a shot or a structural problem, patterns move up and down his forearm.

He makes films that are not quite films â€” immersive experiences designed to be entered via off-brand VR rigs, averaging forty minutes, built from recorded footage of real Highland Park Autonomous Zone life combined with interactive-adjacent decision points that he insists are not choices but pressure â€” moments where the viewer feels the weight of a real person's situation. His work has been passed around on physical data-chips in the HPAZ and has recently started moving through wider underground networks. He is terrified of and fascinated by his growing audience, whom he has never met.

core_fears: That his subjects trust him more than he deserves
That outside success will require him to aestheticize suffering rather than witness it
core_desires: To make a work that changes a specific policy or outcome in the HPAZ
To know whether what he makes is art or journalism and whether it matters
coping_mechanisms: Treats the camera as a mediating object that lets him be present in situations that would otherwise overwhelm him
Obsessive organization of archive footage as a calming ritual
blind_spots: Does not notice when his presence changes the scenes he is documenting
psychology.secret: He has twelve hours of footage documenting what appears to be a Ferrogate Transit contractor performing unauthorized infrastructure modifications inside HPAZ water-systems territory. He has not released it because he cannot determine whether releasing it helps or endangers the community, and the longer he waits the more certain he is the moment has passed. He watches it at least once a week.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and structural when discussing film or community; halting and slightly formal in casual conversation, as if he is always slightly outside his own social moment
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, often with visible pauses where he recalibrates what he was about to say
verbal_tics: 'How do you want toâ€” sorry, let me start again'
Refers to himself in the third person when discussing his work ('Ghost Reel needs to...')
example_lines: 'The piece isn't asking you to feel sympathy. That's too easy. It's asking you to notice the specific moment you looked away and why.'
'I have the footage. I have had the footage for eleven months. That is its own kind of story and I don't know what to do with it yet.'

story_hooks: The twelve hours of Ferrogate Transit footage has been copied without his knowledge â€” someone inside the Booth had access to his archive and he doesn't know who or why.

A prominent Tier 4 arts foundation has made contact through an intermediary offering distribution and funding for his next project, conditional on 'editorial collaboration' â€” and he needs someone to help him understand what that actually means in contract language.
narrative_function: Eyes and ears of the Highland Park Autonomous Zone; documentary record of community life; person who can provide footage or testimony of things that happened; potential unwilling witness to something dangerous
augmentations: Repurposed agricultural color-shift skin mod on right arm (functional/display hybrid); custom optical recording array (heavily modified consumer hardware, basically an augmentation at this point)
daily_life: Spends most of every day either recording â€” following community members with permission, documenting zone infrastructure, capturing ambient data â€” or in the Booth editing and building immersive rigs; eats irregularly, maintains the water tower's operational systems as a rent substitute.
affiliation: Waxwing Neuromedia (mid-level underground filmmaker and vr experience designer)

decision_rules: Always ask permission before recording anyone in a private moment
Do not accept funding from any entity with a stake in the story being told
escalation_ladder: Asks clarifying questions when threatened, buying time
Copies and distributes archive to trusted parties before taking action â€” protects the record first
Goes public with material as a defensive move if cornered

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Slightly formal and careful, asks a lot of questions, more comfortable with a camera between them
interpersonal_modes.friends: Deeply loyal, shows up in practical ways, remembers everything they have ever told him

stress_responses.medium: Reviews archive footage obsessively, especially the Ferrogate material
stress_responses.high: Shuts the Booth and goes dark â€” no comms, just edits for days

contradictions: Believes in radical transparency as a value but has been sitting on the most important footage of his life for almost a year
habits: Keeps a running spoken audio diary on a physical recorder â€” not digital â€” stored in a sealed case
Knows the HPAZ water tower systems better than the original engineers
breaking_points: Discovering that footage of his subjects is being used to harm them
